references.role: STYLE PLATE: four card illustrations in the black-and-gold Art Deco style of this game, cropped from concept art and still standing on their black lacquer card backdrop with small crimson corner triangles. Copy their rendering exactly (polished gold with crisp specular bands, ivory enamel, glossy lacquer, deep crimson and teal enamel, elegant streamlined geometry, fanned gold rays). Do not copy their subjects, their layout, the black backdrop or the corner triangles. The pip colours of the dice on the plate are not a style rule: pips follow the subject.
SUBJECT AND SILHOUETTE REFERENCE ONLY. Match the same tray, outline, projection and rim placement. Reference 1 is the only style reference for colour, material treatment, shading and linework.

generations.revisedPrompt:
Create ONE standalone card-theme illustration. Subject: One empty wide shallow tabletop tray, seen nearly overhead. Match the projected silhouette, angle and proportions of reference 2. Use reference 1 alone for the rendering style. The entire back rim is visible, the two back corners taper slightly inward, and the low near lip casts a narrow contact shadow. Light from upper left. The central bed is a single uninterrupted resting surface for the runtime foreground. Show the complete tray alone on transparent ground with space around all four edges. No cards, dice, pips, letters, numbers, coins, people, emblems, captions, buttons, or artwork outside the silhouette. A black lacquer tray with a narrow gold lip and small symmetrical corner details. Separate the silhouette from a dark table with a restrained rim. Keep gold off the central bed.
Style: Match the STYLE PLATE (reference image 1) exactly: 1920s Art Deco luxury object illustration. Polished gold and brass with crisp specular bands, glossy ivory enamel, black lacquer, and deep crimson and teal enamel inlays; elegant streamlined geometric forms with stepped and fanned motifs; precise thin gold edge lines; rich but restrained, like a jeweller's poster. Dice are ivory-enamel cubes with softly rounded edges and black-lacquer pips; crimson or teal pips only when the subject names red or blue pips. Three-quarter view from slightly above; soft studio light from the upper left with warm gold reflections.
Colour roles: Ivory #F8E5C6 for dice bodies and lit enamel; gold #D9A44E shaded with old gold #B7916B and bronze #785C3E for metal, rims, handles, coins and rays; crimson #7A120C for red pips and red enamel; deep teal #0E4A66 for blue pips, water and blue enamel; black lacquer #15110D only for dark lacquer parts, neutral pips and the deepest shadows. No other hues, no neon, no glow.
Composition: One cohesive subject group of at most three objects, centred on a square canvas; the subject spans roughly 70 to 95 percent of the canvas width without touching the edges, with even transparent margin on every side; the silhouette must stay readable at 64 pixels. Two or three short fanned gold ray strokes are allowed when they express the effect. The card frame of the game draws its own backdrop, so the illustration has no background field at all.
Output: True transparent alpha background with no backdrop of any colour and no background shapes. A single finished illustration, not a sheet of variants.
Avoid: text, letters, numbers, labels, prices, card frames, UI elements, a background field, a black backdrop panel, a sunburst backdrop, corner triangles, ground scenery, reflections of a floor, checkerboard, photorealism, plastic 3D-render look, chrome, pixel art, neon glow, grunge, human characters, expressive faces.
